correctness.summary: Using the structural conclusion in the proof of the current triangle-free Cartesian-product theorem, any hypothetical monophonic position set of size at least three in the product is layered over a leaf and projects to pairwise-distance-two vertices. For twice-subdivided trees these projected vertices share an original branch center, and an explicit 19-vertex induced path passes through any chosen triple. This forces the exact value two.

limitations: No classification of all tree pairs with monophonic position number two is claimed.
Exact twice-subdivision is a sufficient construction, not claimed necessary.
Finite verification is corroborative and not part of the proof.
Originality is to the best of our knowledge and retains residual risk from differently indexed recent work.

originality.scope: to the best of our knowledge
originality.summary: The accessible primary Cartesian-product article and targeted searches under monophonic/induced-path position, tree, subdivision, 2-subdivision, spider, and product terminology did not locate this twice-subdivision theorem or an equivalent stronger statement. Residual risk remains from differently indexed or not-yet-indexed follow-up work.

review_statement: Same-model review: passed. Independent audit: not yet performed.

value.summary: The theorem gives a broad exact family parameterized by arbitrary pairs of trees and shows that the existing triangle-free maximum-degree upper bound can have unbounded slack even when both factors are trees with leaves.
